text.insert: Running is the autonomous scheduling slice for one run inside a project session. RunState binds stable identity and immutable inputs to control status, while the director turns active dispatch authority into epochs and claims. A pending-integration boundary keeps Git lineage and durable session state convergent across a crash.
Run Identity and Inputs

Every run-scoped object is addressed by run_id, so an epoch, claim, worker state, checkpoint, or integration record always names the autonomous effort that owns it. session_id names the containing project session; it never stands in for a run identity.
RunInputs capture the reproducible starting conditions and become immutable when activation accepts them:
base_revision is fixed as the run's original baseline at activation. Later head movement changes the session head mirror, not this origin.
policy_revision is a deterministic digest of the canonical configuration snapshot, so equal policy inputs bind to the same revision.
starting_knowledge_revision is a deterministic digest of the ordered starting knowledge content, so the run records the evidence generation it began from even when background knowledge advances.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — runs survive sync via remote-application boundaries

text.insert: Sync does not replace the interrupted run. The run identity and original base_revision remain fixed while the session head advances through a remote-application boundary.
How a Run Survives Sync

Run continuity separates the effort's fixed origin from the head it plans against. The running slice mirrors the session head and replans from that value after sync; it does not publish remote-application boundaries.

The sync workflow contract owns the remote_application writer and the transaction that publishes the applied upstream revision into session lineage. That writer is outside the implemented running slice.
An active run retains its run_id and references the resulting boundary, while a sync with no active run attaches the boundary to the session alone.
Control State and Scheduling Condition

Run status answers whether autonomous scheduling has authority and whether existing work must settle. The eight values form one control vocabulary; active specifically means the run holds the project dispatch lease.

rows: No scheduler or worker may start.
Required inputs are captured and readiness gates pass.
The run holds the project dispatch lease.
New admission is disabled while admitted work settles.
Scheduling is disabled and the same run remains resumable.
Existing work has settled or been explicitly recovered.
The runner could not safely continue.
Recovery returns this identity to paused.
Evidence remains readable and the run is terminal.
props.title: Run status values

text.insert: scheduler_condition is an observability mirror of what the scheduler is doing inside that control state: idle, planning, dispatching, waiting, boundary, or blocked. It does not replace status, grant dispatch authority, or create another state machine.

Pause is drain-based. A pause request moves active → draining, stops new admission, waits for claims and boundary work to settle, and then records paused; a confirmed hard stop uses recovery to cancel unsettled work before reaching the same paused state.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — failed runs resume in place

text.insert: Recovery never creates a successor run. A failed run returns to paused on the same run_id, and only completed and cancelled are terminal.
How In-Place Recovery Works
Recovery repairs durable boundaries before it changes run control, so the resumed identity never plans from an ambiguous head:
It first reconciles pending epoch integrations, then settles or cancels orphaned claims and breaks a stale dispatch lease when one is still held.
It emits run.recovered with the cancelled claim and operation subject ids, clears the failed control residue, and moves failed → paused on the same run_id.
The operator resumes paused → active through the normal lease acquisition path. Failed remains recoverable or cancellable; completed and cancelled cannot resume.
Pending Integration Boundary
Epoch publication crosses a Git commit boundary and a database transaction boundary. The pending-integration protocol gives reconciliation durable evidence for the only crash window between them:
Before the Git integration commit, the runtime commits a pending_integrations row containing run_id, epoch_id, branch, parent SHA, and the expected message marker.
The integration commit carries the stable Epoch-Integration: <epoch_id> trailer, which identifies the boundary independently of process memory.
The epoch-close transaction records epoch completion, advances the session and run head mirrors, and deletes the pending row in that same transaction.

Startup reconciles pending rows before acquiring dispatch authority, and run recovery reconciles them before settling claims. Both locate the trailer after the recorded parent; a found commit completes the epoch-close transaction, while a missing commit closes the boundary as an integration error and removes the stale row.
